title: Register space of obstruction-free set agreement
formal: For every pair of integers \(n>k\ge1\), determine \(R(n,k)\), the minimum number of atomic read/write registers sufficient for deterministic obstruction-free one-shot \(k\)-set agreement among \(n\) processes with inputs in \([n]\). Supply the resulting function with pointwise absolute error at most \(1/100\) registers.
definitions: An asynchronous shared-memory system has named processes \(1,\ldots,n\), each with one input value, unbounded private computation and private storage, and at most \(r\) shared multiwriter/multireader registers. Each register may hold any finite value; register width is not charged. A shared step is an atomic Read or Write, and no stronger primitive or random choice is available. Every decision must be an input proposed by a participating process, and across an execution at most \(k\) distinct values may be decided. Safety must hold under every schedule, including process crashes. Obstruction-freedom means that from every reachable configuration, a process that thereafter runs alone for sufficiently many own steps decides, regardless of whether other processes ever resume. Each process invokes the task at most once. \(R(n,k)\) is the minimum integer \(r\ge0\) for which such a protocol exists; a protocol may depend on \(n,k\). Inputs, private memory and local computation are uncharged; all shared registers are counted.
why: This measures a basic memory cost of synchronization and exposes a large gap between known impossibility arguments and protocols.

context_blocks.text: Ellen, Gelashvili and Zhu prove \(R(n,k)\ge\lceil n/k\rceil\). A known protocol gives \(R(n,k)\le n-k+1\). The endpoints coincide for consensus but can be far apart as \(k\) grows.
The 2025 source continues to state these register bounds. Bounds for swap objects concern a stronger primitive and do not determine this read/write-register function.

progress.text: The journal paper proves the \(\lceil n/k\rceil\) register lower bound.
The OPODIS paper retains the gap to the n-k+1 register upper bound.

answer_criterion: Supply a real-valued function \(g\) on all integer pairs \(n>k\ge1\), and prove in Lean that \(|g(n,k)-R(n,k)|\le1/100\) throughout the domain, in registers. The approximation need not be integer-valued. A finite table or bounds that do not reach this precision do not determine the function.

The benchmark requests the full register-space function over all n greater than k.
